title: Net-New ARR After a Churn, an Upsell, and a Migration
scenario_text: Constantan Cloud must report net-new ARR for a customer family over FY24, and the number depends on correctly resolving which contracts belong to one continuing entity. The customer entered FY24 with two Salesforce accounts: A-1 "Zamak Media LLC" (EIN 45-1120900) with SUB-1 at $500,000 ARR, and A-2 "Zamak Studios Inc." (EIN 88-3320145) with SUB-2 at $300,000 ARR. During FY24: (a) On 2024-02-01, Zamak Media LLC completed a statutory conversion to "Zamak Media Inc." (new EIN 61-7788092), same business continuing; SUB-1 was novated to the new EIN with NO change in price ($500,000). (b) On 2024-05-01, that same continuing entity signed an upsell add-on SUB-3 for +$200,000 ARR. (c) On 2024-07-01, Zamak Studios Inc. (A-2) churned entirely; SUB-2 ($300,000) was terminated for non-renewal. (d) A data sync created a THIRD Salesforce account A-3 "Zamak Media Inc." for the post-conversion entity, so its ARR ($500,000 + $200,000) appears there while the old A-1 still shows $500,000, double-counting $500,000 if summed naively. Net-new ARR for the year is defined as (upsell/new ARR) minus (churned ARR), excluding pure entity-continuation moves that carry the same revenue (the conversion/novation is not new business). The net-new figure anchors the sales team's quota-retirement and the board's growth narrative, so a double-counted duplicate account or a mistreated statutory conversion would overstate growth materially. The draft dashboard sums all Salesforce accounts naively and shows a large positive number, which the analytics lead suspects hides both an offsetting churn on a separately-EIN'd entity and a phantom continuation entry created by the conversion. The lead must resolve which records represent one continuing entity and which represent genuine new or lost business before reporting the year's net-new ARR.
question: What is the net-new ARR for this customer family in FY24?
